marks.gloss_en: שכן מצינו -- in Shimon ben Shetach's days rain fell on Wednesday and Shabbat nights (kind svara for a 'so we found' precedent; header)
for so we found in the days of Shimon ben Shetach that rain fell for them on Wednesday nights and Shabbat nights, until wheat grew like kidneys, barley like olive pits, and lentils like gold dinars
וכן מצינו -- in Herod's days rain fell only at night, and the people went out to their work by day (kind svara; header)

and so we found in Herod's days, when they were engaged in building the Temple: rain fell at night, next day the wind blew, the clouds scattered and the sun shone, the people went out to their work, and they knew that the work of Heaven was in their hands
alternatively: 'in their season' -- on Wednesday nights and on Shabbat nights
once, most of Adar had passed and no rain had fallen
Choni: Master of the world, Your children have turned to me, for I am like a member of Your household; I swear by Your great name that I will not move from here until You have mercy on Your children
Choni: not thus did I ask, but for rain [to fill] cisterns, ditches and caves
Choni: not thus did I ask, but for rain of favour, blessing and generosity
nevertheless, bring me a bull of thanksgiving; they brought it, and he laid both hands on it

Shimon ben Shatach: were you not Choni, I would decree a ban on you; for were these years like Elijah's, when the keys of rain were in his hand, would not the name of Heaven be desecrated through you?

but what can I do to you, for you importune the Omnipresent and He does your will, as a son importunes his father and he does his will (wash me in hot water, rinse me in cold, give me nuts, almonds, peaches and pomegranates -- and he gives)
what the Chamber of Hewn Stone sent Choni: 'you shall decree a thing and it shall be established for you, and light shall shine on your ways' (Job 22:28)
'you shall decree a thing' -- you decreed below, and the Holy One fulfils your word above
'when they are cast down, you shall say: lift up' (Job 22:29) -- a generation that was low you raised with your prayer
all his life that righteous man was troubled by 'when the Lord returned the captivity of Zion we were like dreamers' (Ps 126:1); he said: is there anyone who sleeps seventy years in a dream?
the man planting a carob, which bears fruit after seventy years: I found the world with carobs; as my fathers planted for me, I too plant for my children
a rock-formation enclosed him, he was hidden from sight and slept seventy years; when he rose he saw a man gathering from [the carobs] -- the planter's grandson
the Sages in the study hall: our teachings are as clear as in the years of Choni HaMe'aggel, for when he entered the study hall he would resolve every difficulty the Sages had
Abba Chilkiya was Choni's grandson; when the world needed rain the Sages would send to him, he would pray, and rain came
